title: Logarithmic and Exponential Equations
seo_title: Precalculus Logarithmic and Exponential Equations Worksheets (TEKS P.5F–P.5H)
standard_text: P.5F use the properties of logarithms to evaluate or transform logarithmic expressions; P.5G generate and solve logarithmic equations in mathematical and real-world problems; P.5H generate and solve exponential equations in mathematical and real-world problems
meta_desc: Free Precalculus worksheets on logarithmic and exponential equations for Texas TEKS P.5F to P.5H: log properties, change of base, solving equations and growth models. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Get the power alone, then take a log of both sides.
key_sub: Check that every log input is positive.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Product: log MN = log M + log N. Quotient: log MN = log M − log N. Power: log Mk = k log M.
  • Change of base: logb x = ln xln b.
  • Exponential equation: get the power alone, then take a log of both sides.
  • Log equation: combine the logs, rewrite in exponential form, and check that every log input is positive.

Examples

Example

1,000(1.05)t = 2,000

1.05t = 2

t = log 2 ÷ log 1.05

Answer: t ≈ 14.2

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
log(M + N) = log M + log NThe product rule is for log MN.
Dividing instead of taking logs1.05t = 2 needs logarithms.
Not checkingA log input must be positive.

faq.a: Use the properties of logarithms to evaluate or transform logarithmic expressions.
Generate and solve logarithmic equations in mathematical and real-world problems.
Generate and solve exponential equations in mathematical and real-world problems.
Any base works; ln and log are on calculators.

items.q: Expand ln x5.
items.e: Power property: bring the exponent to the front as a multiplier. 5 ln x.

items.q: Expand log2 xy.
items.e: Quotient property: the log of a quotient is the difference of the logs, top minus bottom. log2 x − log2 y.

items.q: Expand log5 x5.
items.e: Power property: bring the exponent to the front as a multiplier. 5 log5 x.

items.q: Expand log3 x4yz3.
items.e: Product (add) for the top, quotient (subtract) for the bottom, and power (bring exponents to the front). 4 log3 x + log3 y − 3 log3 z.

items.q: Expand ln x2yz3.
items.e: Product (add) for the top, quotient (subtract) for the bottom, and power (bring exponents to the front). 2 ln x + ln y − 3 ln z.

items.q: Expand log x5.
items.e: Power property: bring the exponent to the front as a multiplier. 5 log x.

items.q: Expand ln x4yz3.
items.e: Product (add) for the top, quotient (subtract) for the bottom, and power (bring exponents to the front). 4 ln x + ln y − 3 ln z.

items.e: Product (add) for the top, quotient (subtract) for the bottom, and power (bring exponents to the front). 4 log5 x + log5 y − 3 log5 z.

items.q: Expand log2 3x.
items.e: Product property: the log of a product is the sum of the logs. log2 3 + log2 x.

items.q: Expand log xy.
items.e: Quotient property: the log of a quotient is the difference of the logs, top minus bottom. log x − log y.

items.q: Simplify log3 3 + log3 27.
items.e: Product property: log3 (3 × 27) = log3 81 = 4.

items.q: Write as a single logarithm: 3 log3 x + log3 y − 3 log3 z.
items.e: Move the multipliers up as exponents, then add means multiply and subtract means divide. log3 x3yz3.

items.q: Write as a single logarithm: 2 ln x + ln y − 4 ln z.
items.e: Move the multipliers up as exponents, then add means multiply and subtract means divide. ln x2yz4.

items.q: Simplify log2 20 − log2 5.
items.e: Quotient property: log2 205 = log2 4 = 2.

items.q: Simplify log2 56 − log2 7.
items.e: Quotient property: log2 567 = log2 8 = 3.

items.q: Simplify log 2 + log 50.
items.e: Product property: log (2 × 50) = log 100 = 2.

items.q: Write 2 log 3 as a single logarithm.
items.e: Power property in reverse: 2 log 3 = log 32 = log 9.

items.q: Write as a single logarithm: 3 ln x + ln y − 2 ln z.
items.e: Move the multipliers up as exponents, then add means multiply and subtract means divide. ln x3yz2.

items.q: Simplify log 200 − log 2.
items.e: Quotient property: log 2002 = log 100 = 2.

items.q: Write as a single logarithm: 2 log3 x + log3 y − 2 log3 z.
items.e: Move the multipliers up as exponents, then add means multiply and subtract means divide. log3 x2yz2.

items.q: What is the inverse of f(x) = 10x?
items.e: Swap x and y: x = 10y. In log form, y = log x. f−1(x) = log x.

items.q: What is the inverse of f(x) = 3x?
items.e: Swap x and y: x = 3y. In log form, y = log3 x. f−1(x) = log3 x.

items.q: What is the inverse of f(x) = 2x?
items.e: Swap x and y: x = 2y. In log form, y = log2 x. f−1(x) = log2 x.

items.q: What is the inverse of f(x) = 5x?
items.e: Swap x and y: x = 5y. In log form, y = log5 x. f−1(x) = log5 x.

items.q: Which expression equals log4 11?
items.e: Change of base: logb x = (ln x) ÷ (ln b). ln 11ln 4.

items.q: Which expression equals log3 20?
items.e: Change of base: logb x = (ln x) ÷ (ln b). ln 20ln 3.

items.q: What is the domain of f(x) = log2 (x − 5)?
items.e: You can only take the log of a positive number: x − 5 > 0. x > 5. The graph has a vertical asymptote at x = 5.

items.q: Which expression equals log2 9?
items.e: Change of base: logb x = (ln x) ÷ (ln b). ln 9ln 2.

items.q: Solve e12x = 20. Round to the nearest thousandth.
items.e: Take ln of both sides: 12x = ln 20, so x = ln 20 ÷ 12 ≈ 5.991.

items.q: Solve 2x = 20. Round to the nearest thousandth.
items.e: Take the log of both sides: x log 2 = log 20, so x = log 20 ÷ log 2 ≈ 4.322.

items.q: Solve 2 · 2x + 7 = 37. Round to the nearest thousandth.
items.e: Isolate the power first: 2x = (37 − 7) ÷ 2 = 15. Then x = log(15) ÷ log 2 ≈ 3.907.

items.q: Solve 3x = 15. Round to the nearest thousandth.
items.e: Take the log of both sides: x log 3 = log 15, so x = log 15 ÷ log 3 ≈ 2.465.

items.q: Solve 3x = 10. Round to the nearest thousandth.
items.e: Take the log of both sides: x log 3 = log 10, so x = log 10 ÷ log 3 ≈ 2.096.

items.q: Solve 7x = 40. Round to the nearest thousandth.

items.q: Solve 2x = 50. Round to the nearest thousandth.

items.q: Solve 5x = 10. Round to the nearest thousandth.

items.q: Solve e2x = 30. Round to the nearest thousandth.
items.e: Take ln of both sides: 2x = ln 30, so x = ln 30 ÷ 2 ≈ 1.701.

items.q: Solve 2x = 200. Round to the nearest thousandth.
items.e: Take the log of both sides: x log 2 = log 200, so x = log 200 ÷ log 2 ≈ 7.644.

items.q: Solve 23x − 3 = 64.
items.e: Write 64 as 26. Set the exponents equal: 3x − 3 = 6, so x = 3.

items.q: Solve 9x = 27x − 2.
items.e: Rewrite with base 3: 32x = 33(x − 2). So 2x = 3x − 6 and x = 6.

items.q: Solve 4x = 32x − 1.
items.e: Rewrite with base 2: 22x = 25(x − 1). So 2x = 5x − 5 and x = 53.

items.q: Solve 33x + 2 = 81.
items.e: Write 81 as 34. Set the exponents equal: 3x + 2 = 4, so x = 23.

items.q: Solve 52x + 2 = 25.
items.e: Write 25 as 52. Set the exponents equal: 2x + 2 = 2, so x = 0.

items.q: Solve 32x + 4 = 27.

Sound level in decibels is L = 10 log(I/I0). If one sound is 20 dB louder than another, how many times as intense is it?
items.e: A difference of 20 dB means log(ratio) = 20 ÷ 10 = 2, so the ratio is 102 = 100 times.

items.q: Mia invests $1,000 at 5% compounded monthly. After how many years will the balance first reach $2,500? Round to the nearest tenth.
items.e: 1,000(1 + 0.05/12)12t = 2,500, so 12t = log(52) ÷ log(1 + 0.05/12) and t ≈ 18.4 years.

items.q: How long does it take money to double at 7% interest compounded annually? Round to the nearest tenth of a year.
items.e: Solve (1.07)t = 2: t = log 2 ÷ log 1.07 ≈ 10.2 years.
